output_md:
Yesterday, a tech texts in sick at 7:14 and eight jobs now belong to nobody. The morning has been a string of calls to reassign them; everyone is scrambling as the SLA clocks tick down.

The problem isn't the people—the techs are competent and always trying to help. It’s the data they have to work with. Without a clear view of travel times, skills required, and how many other jobs are coming up, no one knows what to do next. The tech has the right skills, but he's got a 45-minute commute. And three of those eight jobs just hit their SLA clock.

Here’s what changes: with Slatebridge, when that tech texts in sick, we see his skills and routes instantly. We know if anyone else can cover. If not, I see the work piling up, and I have time to find a solution before the SLAs are missed.

So what's your biggest scheduling headache? Comment below—do you blame it on people or data?
